root_cause.text: In the i915 DRM display power-management code, `gen9_set_dc_state()` and `intel_dmc_get_dc6_allowed_count()` incorrectly used the current hardware DC6 state (`DC_STATE_EN`) to decide whether to call `intel_dmc_update_dc6_allowed_count()`, so at probe they could invoke it before `intel_dmc_init()` had set up `dmc`, causing a NULL dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `dc6_was_enabled = val & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6;` to `power_domains->dc_state & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6;` in `gen9_set_dc_state()`, and similarly replaces `intel_de_read(display, DC_STATE_EN)` with `power_domains->dc_state` in `intel_dmc_get_dc6_allowed_count()`, while the CVE text states that `intel_power_domains_init_hw()` runs before `intel_dmc_init()`, so `intel_dmc_update_dc6_allowed_count()` can be called when `dmc` is still NULL.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DC6 transition detection by comparing against the cached power-domain state instead of the raw register value.
intent_record.what: In gen9_set_dc_state(), the assignment to dc6_was_enabled was changed from reading the hardware register value 'val & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6' to reading the cached software state 'power_domains->dc_state & DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6'.
intent_record.how: This makes the DC6 enablement comparison use the previously tracked state instead of the current register value, so the code can correctly detect a transition from DC6-disabled to DC6-enabled and update the DMC DC6 allowed count at the right time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the cached power-domain DC state when checking DC6 enablement instead of rereading the hardware register.
intent_record.what: In intel_dmc_get_dc6_allowed_count(), the dc6_enabled assignment was changed from reading the DC_STATE_EN register via intel_de_read(display, DC_STATE_EN) masked with DC_STATE_EN_UPTO_DC6 to using the cached power_domains->dc_state value masked with the same bitfield.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now determines whether DC6 is enabled from the power domain's stored state instead of performing a fresh hardware register read, which makes the check rely on the tracked software state and avoids an extra MMIO read.

grouping_result.intent: Use the cached power-domain DC state when checking DC6 enablement instead of rereading the hardware register.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement rereads the live hardware DC_STATE_EN register instead of using cached power-domain state, which could report DC6 as enabled during probe before intel_dmc_init() has initialized dmc, leading to the unsafe path that dereferences it.

This line derives prior DC6 enablement from the raw hardware register value rather than the cached state, making the transition logic incorrect and allowing intel_dmc_update_dc6_allowed_count() to be called before dmc is ready.

This conditional is the decision point that triggers the DMC update; because dc6_was_enabled was based on the current hardware register, it could incorrectly evaluate as a transition during probe and invoke the update too early.
This is the call that can dereference dmc; once the preceding hardware-state check incorrectly indicates DC6 is enabled, this function can run before intel_dmc_init() has initialized the pointer.
